name: tm_barrier_domain
code:
def tm_barrier_domain(p, hw, cfg) -> float:
    """log2 of the warps one mainloop barrier effectively waits on: the CTA's own warps when operands move as 16-byte cp.async (L1 bypassed, CTAs independent); every warp resident on the SM when alignment forces narrower copies through the L1 that co-resident CTAs share. Larger is worse."""
    T = math.ceil(p.M / cfg.tile_m) * math.ceil(p.N / cfg.tile_n)
    n = math.ceil(T * max(1, cfg.split_k) / hw.sm_count)
    res = max(1, min(n, cfg.max_blocks_per_sm))
    vec = min(cfg.align_a, cfg.align_b) * p.bytes_per_element
    coupled = 1.0 if vec < 16 else 0.0
    return math.log2(max(1.0, cfg.threads / 32.0)) + coupled * math.log2(res)
rationale: Each mainloop iteration ends in a CTA-wide barrier that also waits on that iteration's cp.async group; its expected stall grows like the log of the number of warps whose arrivals it waits on (tm_cta_warps). 16 is cp.async's largest copy in bytes and the only size the L1-bypassing .cg form accepts (PTX ISA, not a GPU value). With 16-byte operand copies each CTA streams L2->smem on its own, so co-resident CTAs are separate barrier domains and the charge is log2(warps per CTA): measured on fold-train shapes, 128x128x32 with 128 threads x 2 CTAs/SM beats 256 threads x 1 CTA/SM by a median 0.22 log2 over 57 shapes, so equal warps per SM are NOT equivalent there. When the operand alignment forces narrower copies they must use cp.async.ca, which stages through the L1 that all resident CTAs share; their copy groups then drain through one fill path and the barriers couple, so the domain is every warp resident on the SM: log2(warps per CTA x resident CTAs), which charges configs with equal warps per SM equally (1024x4096x4100, align 4: 256 threads x 1 CTA is best, 128 threads x 2 CTAs is 1.17-1.20). Resident CTAs = min(SM-granular CTAs per SM, max_blocks_per_sm). Pool note: replaces tm_cta_warps; identical to it on every 16-byte-aligned shape, so its alignment branch is identified by only two fold-train shapes (1024x4096x4098, 4100).
